messages.subject: Re: RPostgreSQL transactions
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The point 2 is perhaps mostly done with the last commit r230.
Probably,
dbGetQuery(con, "BEGIN TRANSACTION")
will work fine. 

A small test was added as dbTransactionTests.R
at r228, and you can see how it works.

I appreciate, if you have some test on it and report if any problem
exists.

Whether to make it under the name of dbBeginTransaction()
remain as a matter of the standardization of DBI. 

Best regards,
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan


On 2012/03/29, at 16:58, Willem Ligtenberg wrote:

> Hi,
> 
> It is a pity that it has been dropped, since it is a nice feature of a
> database system like Postgresql.
> I am not sure if it is common enough that it has to be in DBI,
> although MySQL also support it and quite probably that is one of the
> most used systems.
> I understand why you dropped it, but I really do hope to see the
> feature return in future releases. (And probably also supported in
> DBI)
> 
> Kind regards,
> 
> Willem
> 
> On Wed, Mar 28, 2012 at 14:51, Tomoaki NISHIYAMA
> <tomoakin-mW12fOdZGSDdqfzlIRWTy7hJywXYPV/v at public.gmane.org> wrote:
>> Hi,
>> 
>> Thank you for comments.
>> 
>> dbBeginTransaction() was dropped recently because
>> 1. it is not defined in DBI
>> 2. RPostgreSQL code base did not guarantee the
>>   communication is done through a single connection
>> 
>> While both are not simple problems,
>> I cannot directly change the DBI specification.
>> If necessary, please contact DBI maintainers.
>> To my understanding, the DBI standard expects transaction mode /
>> autocommit mode may be set as an option at connection rather than a function
>> like dbBeginTransaction(). RMySQL implemented dbBeginTransaction() and
>> RPostgreSQL originally inherited it.  But when you load both libraries (for sqldf),
>> a warning was emitted.
>> 
>> For the point 2, there are following code in a few places:
>> 
>>    ## Do we need to clone the connection (ie., if it is in use)?
>>    if(length(dbListResults(con))!=0){
>>        new.con <- dbConnect(con)              ## there's pending work, so clone
>>        on.exit(dbDisconnect(new.con))
>>    }
>>    else
>>        new.con <- con
>> 
>> When this code is executed and cloned, perhaps you will see different things
>> in different queries in transaction mode. I have a code with these removed
>> but did not have confidence to commit as I do not have a good test method yet.
>> 
>> If you code very carefully so that the second channel would not
>> be opened,
>> dbGetQuery(con, "BEGIN transaction")
>> would start a transaction.
>> dbGetQuery() after dbSendQuery() without fetching all the results
>> is perhaps the trigger of the clone connection.
>> 
>> It is my mistake that dbBeginTransaction() remained in some documents without warning,
>> but please understand that it is likely very unstable if it was kept.
>> 
>> If you want to test a version with the connection cloning disabled, I will
>> commit to the svn tree as soon as possible. (see http://code.google.com/p/rpostgresql/)
>> 
>> Best regards,
>> --
>> Tomoaki NISHIYAMA
>> 
>> Advanced Science Research Center,
>> Kanazawa University,
>> 13-1 Takara-machi,
>> Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan
>> 
>> 
>> On 2012/03/28, at 21:11, Willem Ligtenberg wrote:
>> 
>>> Hi,
>>> 
>>> I want to use transactions in postgresql from within R.
>>> When I look at the manual I can find the following method:
>>> dbBeginTransaction(con)
>>> 
>>> in the following code:
>>> 
>>> drv <- dbDriver("PostgreSQL")
>>> con <- dbConnect(drv, dbname="postgres")
>>> dbGetQuery(con, "select count(*) from sales")
>>> dbBeginTransaction(con)
>>> rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "Delete * from sales as p where p.cost>10")
>>> if(dbGetInfo(rs, what = "rowsAffected") > 250){
>>>  warning("Rolling back transaction")
>>>  dbRollback(con)
>>> }
>>> dbGetQuery(con, "select count(*) from sales")
>>> dbDisconnect(con)
>>> 
>>> However, when I try to use that method with versionL RPostgreSQL_0.3-1
>>> I get the following error:
>>> Error in function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
>>>  unable to find an inherited method for function
>>> "dbBeginTransaction", for signature "PostgreSQLConnection"
>>> 
>>> Does this mean that it is currently not possible to use transaction
>>> from within R?
>>> 
>>> Kind regards,
>>> 
>>> Willem
>>
